meaning: K1 RC1 is a narrow semantic court over precommitted source-admissible consequences and proof-established target-realizable consequences. It is not a source parser, temporal prover, implementation semantics engine, or repair synthesizer.

semantic_objects.W: nonempty set of admitted world commitments
semantic_objects.U: open universe of canonical consequence commitments
semantic_objects.ALLOW: precommitted source-admissible relation, subset of W x U, nonempty per admitted world
semantic_objects.REALIZE: target-realizable relation established by an accepted proof object

verdict_rules.REGRESSION: One accepted locally grounded pair in REALIZE minus ALLOW is semantically sufficient.
verdict_rules.PRESERVATION: Requires accepted closure/exhaustiveness for the exact declared target scope, grounding for every realized pair, per-world consequential-cut totality, and REALIZE subset-of ALLOW.
verdict_rules.UNKNOWN: Any missing closure, grounding, totality, interpretation, or proof-scope support is neither regression nor preservation.

constitutional_invariants: SOURCE_FIRST_COMMITMENT: W and ALLOW are fixed before target realization is inspected.
NO_POSTHOC_AMNESTY: a forbidden realized consequence cannot be added to ALLOW without changing claim identity.
NO_POSTHOC_WORLD_SPLIT: target outcomes cannot retrospectively refine source worlds without changing claim identity.
OPEN_CONSEQUENCE_UNIVERSE: target-native consequences may appear in REALIZE even when absent from source vocabulary.
NO_VACUITY: empty world scope, empty per-world source permission, silent consequential cuts, or incomplete closure cannot prove preservation.
GROUNDING: producer assertions alone are not semantic authority.
ASYMMETRY: one grounded forbidden witness can prove regression; absence of found witnesses cannot prove preservation.
IDENTITY_SEPARATION: source claim identity and target realization identity are distinct commitments.
MATERIAL_FIELD_SENSITIVITY: source-declared material world/consequence fields must affect semantic commitment identity.
PROOF_SCOPE_HONESTY: a proof kind may discharge only the semantic scope it actually establishes.
DIAGNOSTIC_NON_AUTHORITY: C/D/O/Exact and other diagnostics cannot strengthen a K1 semantic verdict merely by being present.
MODEL_BOUNDARY_HONESTY: preservation in a declared proof model is not automatically an implementation-binding claim.
not_kernel_primitives: source semantic digest as a universal object

primitive_promotion_rule.required_evidence: A minimal semantic counterexample showing that a required distinction collapses under every admissible target-independent lowering into W, open consequence commitments, ALLOW/REALIZE, and accepted proof obligations.
insufficient_evidence: A current proof kind cannot establish the relation.
A frontend cannot yet compile the source contract.
A diagnostic decomposition is useful for explanation.
A more expressive solver would be convenient.
A domain uses time, authorization, money, history, or information flow.

known_non_kernel_gaps.detail: k1.finite-model/v1 does not establish unbounded trace liveness. Arbitrarily introducing a finite deadline changes source identity. No new semantic kernel primitive is justified by A1.

The abstract K1 regression rule is locally sufficient, but W1 finite-model/v1 currently requires unrelated-world totality because its witness is grounded through a full finite model. A future local-witness proof kind may remove this proof-layer overconstraint.
W1 reports implementation_binding=false. Future proof kinds/evidence must bind declared target models to implementations without enlarging the semantic kernel unless a counterexample requires it.

release_rule: RC1 may be created only after the composite RC1 verifier confirms all pinned dependency blobs and reruns the local qualification commands successfully. RC1 is scoped, not a universal-completeness claim.
